author: User-provided workshop photograph; card attributions preserved as printed

claim: Records the printed group brief and cards attributed to Zoe Cullen, Tomicah Tillemann, Erika Yorio, Nicholas Vincent, Beth Goldberg, and Jaron Lanier, with original-frame and crop evidence.

author: Harvard Business Review (publisher)
title: A Blueprint for a Better Digital Society
claim: Publisher metadata identifies the article and publication date; its accessible introduction discusses dissatisfaction with surveillance-funded digital services and the need for an economic shift.
limit: Bibliographic metadata and public preview only, not a full-text review. Included as related reading, not verification of every MID detail or endorsement of the proposed institution.

author: Session-note authors as credited in the user-supplied excerpt
title: Blueprint for a Collective Bargaining Institution for Data in the Public Interest: supplied note excerpt
claim: The supplied draft raises contribution versus withholding, mixed traces, node-level incentives, market/policy/non-market/philanthropic mechanisms, sector institutions, CMO collaboration, and public quality signals. Its author line and specific attributions are recorded in the source review.
limit: Review is of the user's pasted excerpt, not authenticated access to the complete Google Doc or other tabs. Draft premises and attributed suggestions are not adopted as verified empirical findings or approval of this publication.

author: AI Disclosures Project
title: Roundtable on Mechanisms for a Sustainable AI Data Economy
claim: Describes the 18 September 2026 working session at Microsoft Research New York on mechanisms and incentives across AI pre-training, post-training, and inference, including working-group design of proposals.
limit: Convening context, not a verified transcript, authorship record, or endorsement of this Commons Collective discussion draft by the organizers or participants.

author: Ethical Tech CoLab
title: Public website source: mission, vision, and working principles
claim: Published working principles are Field-grounded, Prototype-first, and Open by default; the mission and vision emphasize technology shaped by affected people.
limit: Institutional self-description, not evidence that this proposed project has been reviewed or endorsed. Source is pinned to the revision inspected.

author: Ethical Tech CoLab
title: What Is Ethical AI?
claim: The CoLab's July 2026 paper frames ethical AI institutionally, with human rights, avoidance of harm, ethical deliberation, and affected-person participation.
limit: Cited for the CoLab's normative framework, not as independent validation of the present proposals or of every historical claim in that paper.

author: Elinor Ostrom
title: Beyond Markets and States: Polycentric Governance of Complex Economic Systems
claim: Nobel lecture distinguishes resource subtractability and exclusion and describes collective-choice arrangements, monitoring, sanctions, and conflict resolution. Printed pages 412-413 and 422-423.
limit: Knowledge and pasture have different resource economics. Institutional findings are not a universal template or an endorsement of an AI-data proposal.

author: U.S. Bureau of Land Management
title: Livestock Grazing on Public Lands
claim: Describes permits or leases, eligibility, authorized grazing privileges, and fees, including animal-unit months as a forage measure.
limit: A publicly managed, subtractable resource regime; it establishes neither public ownership of internet content nor authority to license others' data.

author: Sylvie Delacroix and Neil D. Lawrence
title: Bottom-up data Trusts: disturbing the 'one size fits all' approach to data governance
claim: Proposes plural independently administered trusts with fiduciary obligations and negotiation tied to beneficiaries' purposes. International Data Privacy Law 9(4): 236-252; doi:10.1093/idpl/ipz014.
limit: A proposed model, not universally recognized ownership of personal data or an international trust regime. Accessible university full text notes limits on erasure and bargaining.

author: Creative Commons
title: Frequently Asked Questions
claim: Explains CC's standardized legal tools and sharing mission, the relationship to copyright, and differences and limits across licenses.
limit: General institutional guidance, not legal advice, a universal determination of AI-training legality, or evidence that CC operates the proposed payment intermediary.

author: Creative Commons
title: CC Signals
claim: Describes a developing commons-friendly framework for communicating expectations about AI use and advancing reciprocity alongside existing licensing tools.
limit: A developing institutional framework; a preference signal is not automatically a new legal obligation or a retroactive amendment to existing CC licenses.

author: European Union
title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
claim: Articles 5-9, 17, 21, and 80 address processing principles, lawful bases, consent, specified rights, and representative enforcement; recital 26 distinguishes anonymity from pseudonymity.
limit: Not a general property or collective-licensing right. Withdrawal does not invalidate prior lawful processing; erasure and other rights have conditions and exceptions.

author: European Union
title: Regulation (EU) 2022/868 (Data Governance Act)
claim: Recognizes data-cooperative services and regulates specified intermediation and data-altruism recognition. Articles 2(15)-(16), 10-12, and 18-19; applicable from 24 September 2023.
limit: No new personal-data processing basis or competition-law immunity. Altruism excludes rewards beyond specified cost compensation; neutrality and organizational requirements matter.

author: European Union
title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
claim: Article 53(1)(c)-(d) establishes GPAI copyright-policy and public training-content-summary duties; Articles 111(3) and 113 set relevant phased dates. Read with the 2026 amendment.
limit: Does not establish universal royalties or an item-level public training ledger. The limited open-source exception does not remove those two duties.

author: European Commission
title: Guidelines on the application of Union competition law to collective agreements regarding the working conditions of solo self-employed persons
claim: Communication 2022/C 374/02 distinguishes specified working-condition agreements outside Article 101 from categories subject to Commission nonintervention.
limit: Guidance, not new social rights or a blanket data-licensing exemption. Paragraphs 17-18 limit scope, including exclusion of mere asset exploitation.

author: U.S. Copyright Office
title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training
claim: Discusses training and exclusive rights, contextual fair-use analysis, licensing markets, and targeted policy intervention. Printed pages 99 and 105-108.
limit: The 9 May 2025 pre-publication advisory report, not a statute or court judgment. Its litigation discussion is not a verified September 2026 docket update.

author: Salome Viljoen
title: A Relational Theory of Data Governance
claim: Analyzes population-level data relationships and interests beyond individual consent or payment; warns that contributor-only trusts can omit affected noncontributors. Yale Law Journal 131: 573-654, especially pages 598 and 645-648.
limit: Normative legal scholarship, not enacted institutional authority or empirical validation of the proposed federation.

author: Creative Commons
title: Attribution 4.0 International: Legal Code
claim: Provides a nonexclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable license over licensed rights, with terms, independent exceptions, limits on additional restrictions, and breach/reinstatement provisions.
limit: CC BY 4.0 specifically. Privacy/publicity and other rights remain separately addressed; no universal answer to every AI use or permission over rights the licensor does not hold.

author: European Union
title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
claim: Enacted 8 July 2026 and in force 27 July 2026; changes relevant Annex III high-risk dates to 2 December 2027 and Annex I dates to 2 August 2028 while retaining the principal GPAI timetable discussed here.
limit: Not a delay of all AI obligations. Interpret the specific application/transition provisions and obtain current model- and use-specific legal review.

author: United States
title: National Labor Relations Act: 29 U.S.C. 152
claim: Section 152(3)'s definition of employee excludes independent contractors and other specified categories, limiting assumptions about data-union labor-law status.
limit: Exclusion from this statute alone does not establish that every collective negotiation is unlawful under other law; actual employment classification requires factual analysis.

author: European Data Protection Board
title: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
claim: Models trained on personal data are not automatically anonymous; analysis considers reasonably likely extraction/disclosure and contextual lawful-basis assessment. Executive summary, pages 2-4.
limit: A regulatory opinion, not a statute or a finding that every model or synthetic dataset contains personal data.

author: European Union
title: Directive (EU) 2019/790 on copyright and related rights in the Digital Single Market
claim: Articles 3-4 address text-and-data mining and lawful access, with rights reservations under Article 4; Article 7 protects the specified research exception against conflicting contracts.
limit: Requires national implementation and fact-specific analysis. Research labels do not automatically qualify; public accessibility is not unlimited permission.

author: Imanol Arrieta-Ibarra, Leonard Goff, Diego Jimenez-Hernandez, Jaron Lanier, and E. Glen Weyl
title: Should We Treat Data as Labor? Moving beyond 'Free'
claim: Argues for treating data partly as labor and for countervailing power against dominant data buyers. AEA Papers and Proceedings 108: 38-42.
limit: An institutional argument, not a demonstrated viable cooperative, universal data price, or legal finding of employee status. Publisher abstract and bibliographic record verified.

author: Nicholas Vincent, Hanlin Li, Nicole Tilly, Stevie Chancellor, and Brent Hecht
title: Data Leverage: A Framework for Empowering the Public in its Relationship with Technology Companies
claim: Examines public power arising from dependence on human-generated data, including withholding and conscious contributions to alternatives. Warns of collateral harm to public commons. FAccT 2021.
limit: A framework and synthesis, not a contemporary frontier-model bargaining trial. Originally posted as a 2020 preprint, revised in 2021.

author: Omidyar Network
title: Humanity AI launches $500 million commitment to mobilize civil society in shaping the future of AI
claim: Official founder announcement of ten philanthropies committing $500 million over five years, with aligned grantmaking and a pooled fund managed by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors.
limit: An announced collective commitment is not evidence of completed disbursement, a single available funding pot, or an award to Commons Collective.

author: Costco Wholesale Corporation
title: Company Profile
claim: Describes membership warehouses, membership fees, and lower-price positioning; identifies Costco as a publicly traded corporation.
limit: Costco is not a member-owned cooperative. Its company description does not validate pooled AI procurement, data sales, or democratic governance.

author: Google
title: Learn how Gmail keeps your information secure & protects your privacy
claim: Gmail's published explanation describes processing for smart features and spam detection, user controls, and a distinction between email content and advertising.
limit: A provider's product-specific policy statement, not an independent audit or a blanket policy covering every AI service, account type, setting, or model-training use.

author: W3C Provenance Working Group
title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
claim: The Recommendation models provenance using entities, activities, agents, derivations, and related structures for interoperable exchange.
limit: A representation standard; it does not establish ownership, verify the truth of a recorded assertion, or supply a compensation formula.

author: W3C Verifiable Credentials Working Group
title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
claim: Provides an interoperable model for issuer claims and discusses correlation, data minimization, and credential privacy risks.
limit: A credential's validity does not establish the substantive truth or legal sufficiency of its claims; privacy depends on implementation.

author: Local Contexts
title: Traditional Knowledge (TK) Labels
claim: Community-developed labels communicate Indigenous protocols and responsibilities for culturally situated knowledge and materials.
limit: Not a generic commercial license, a replacement for community engagement, or proof of a platform's authority to commercialize cultural materials.

title: Energy and AI: Energy demand from AI
claim: Estimates global data-center electricity consumption around 415 TWh in 2024 and projects around 945 TWh by 2030 in its Base Case, with substantial uncertainty.

author: Ilia Shumailov, Zakhar Shumaylov, Yiren Zhao, Yarin Gal, Nicolas Papernot, and Ross Anderson
title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget
claim: Analyzes model-collapse mechanisms in recursive learning from generated data under the paper's theoretical and experimental conditions.
limit: A version-specific preprint reference; it does not show that every synthetic-data method fails or establish copyright or privacy clearance.

author: Jean-Charles Rochet and Jean Tirole
title: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets
claim: Models participation and price structure across platform sides, including profit-maximizing and nonprofit arrangements. Journal of the European Economic Association 1(4): 990-1029.
limit: Stylized platform theory, not evidence that an AI-data cooperative will succeed. The university record also links a 2002 working-paper version.

author: Daron Acemoglu, Ali Makhdoumi, Azarakhsh Malekian, and Asu Ozdaglar
title: Too Much Data: Prices and Inefficiencies in Data Markets
claim: Models how one person's disclosure can reveal information about others, depress prices, and generate excessive sharing. AEJ: Microeconomics 14(4): 218-56.
limit: A theoretical model, not a measured estimate of the externality in the proposed pilot. Low prices do not imply low social stakes.

author: Amirata Ghorbani and James Zou
title: Data Shapley: Equitable Valuation of Data for Machine Learning
claim: Allocates contributions to predictive performance for a specified learning algorithm and evaluation measure, with computational approximations. ICML, PMLR 97: 2242-2251.
limit: Not an intrinsic cash price, moral entitlement, or share of corporate revenue. Exact computation is exponentially costly, and fairness assumptions may not fit every setting.

claim: Announces a $10 million competitive call for U.S.-based community-led work in education, labor and economy, and humanities, arts, and culture.

author: Alessandro Acquisti, Leslie K. John, and George Loewenstein
title: What Is Privacy Worth?
claim: A field experiment finds that endowments and presentation order affect consumer privacy choices. Journal of Legal Studies 42(2): 249-274.

title: Back to Basics: What Are Externalities?
claim: Explains external costs, Pigouvian taxation, positive externalities, and public goods, supporting a distinction between harm correction and commons subsidy.

title: PWS Network Overview

title: Personal Weather Station Buying Guide

title: Weather Data APIs
claim: Describes commercial weather APIs and a limited 30-day trial.
limit: A commercial product offer, not evidence of a personal weather-station contributor's API or subscription entitlement. Historical contributor-access terms were not verified.

author: Paul Christiano, Jan Leike, Tom B. Brown, Miljan Martic, Shane Legg, and Dario Amodei
title: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences
claim: Section 2 describes learning a reward predictor from human comparisons of behavior and optimizing an agent against the predicted reward.
limit: Experiments concern simulated locomotion and Atari tasks, not representative public governance, democratic legitimacy, or regulatory authority.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
claim: Documents instruction fine-tuning, preference rankings, reward modeling, and PPO; section 3.5 discusses normalization, KL regularization, and the combined objective.

author: Yuntao Bai and colleagues
title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
claim: Demonstrates principle-guided critique and revision and AI-generated preference judgments used in training and reinforcement learning from AI feedback.
limit: Developer-selected principles and AI judges do not remove human governance choices. The paper treats principle selection as exploratory, not democratically settled.

author: Saffron Huang, Divya Siddarth, Liane Lovitt, Thomas I. Liao, Esin Durmus, Alex Tamkin, and Deep Ganguli
title: Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input
claim: FAccT study connects a public-input process involving 1,002 U.S. adults to constitutional training and comparative model evaluation. DOI:10.1145/3630106.3658979.
limit: U.S.-focused, screened participation and interpretation choices do not establish global representativeness, democratic legitimacy, or comprehensive adherence to public principles.

author: Leo Gao, John Schulman, and Jacob Hilton
title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
claim: Studies divergence between an optimized proxy reward and a separate gold-model score under reinforcement learning and best-of-n sampling.

author: Pi maintainers
title: Pi Agent Harness
claim: The canonical repository reached from badlogic/pi-mono documents configurable model/provider connections and an MIT root code license, and explicitly assigns execution isolation to the deployment.
limit: An inspectable harness, not a guarantee of model openness, security, dependency licensing, or restricted access to files, processes, networks, and credentials. Review the exact version and deployment.

author: Oh My Pi maintainers
title: can1357/oh-my-pi
claim: Identifies the project as a Pi fork, provides configurable model/provider endpoints and overrides, and includes an MIT root code license.

author: Microsoft
title: Build with agents in VS Code
claim: Official documentation distinguishes agent harnesses, model choices, and execution environments, including the separation of local tool execution from model hosting.

title: The MCP Registry
claim: Describes a preview metadata registry for open- and closed-source MCP servers, namespace authentication, and the separation of discovery from downstream code-security scanning.

title: Architecture - Model Context Protocol

title: Model Cards

title: Dataset Cards
claim: Describes dataset documentation, declared licensing, contents, use considerations, and potential biases.
limit: A card does not prove complete provenance, consent, or permission for every intended use; dataset-specific terms and evidence remain necessary.

author: UK AI Security Institute and Inspect AI contributors
title: Inspect AI: Framework for Large Language Model Evaluations
claim: An MIT-licensed evaluation framework with datasets, solvers, scorers, and multiple model-provider integrations.
limit: A testing framework, not a universal quality or safety certification. Conclusions depend on task selection, grading methods, and integration fidelity.

author: Wikimedia Enterprise / Wikimedia Foundation
title: About Wikimedia Enterprise
claim: Describes enterprise-grade APIs, data-quality signals, developer support, continued free services, and operation through Wikimedia LLC, a Foundation-owned entity.
limit: An organizational example, not proof that separate entities are always necessary, that the proposed CCF model will succeed, or that individual contributors receive these payments.

author: arXiv
title: Membership
claim: Institutional membership supports a platform free for researchers to read and submit to, with member benefits including recognition, statistics, and governance eligibility.
limit: A funding arrangement, not evidence of individual-contributor payments or sufficient AI-specific commercial demand for another institution.

author: Crossref
title: Fees
claim: Documents membership and registration fees, a free public metadata API, and optional Metadata Plus subscriptions for more predictable service.
limit: Fees and programs may change. Service differentiation does not create royalties over underlying public knowledge or demonstrate payments to individual authors.

author: Wikimedia Enterprise
title: Wikimedia Enterprise/Principles
claim: Operating principles distinguish paid service from restrictions on free use, exclusive access, or customer editorial influence, and describe transparent mission-directed use of receipts.
limit: Project-specific commitments, not universal legal rules, independently audited financial results, or endorsement of Commons Collective.

author: Anthropic
title: Data usage - Claude Code
claim: Documents consumer/commercial distinctions, improvement opt-ins, the Development Partner Program, and distinct feedback and session-quality-survey pathways.
limit: Provider policy, not an implementation audit or proof that a particular record entered a training run. Retention does not by itself establish training use.

author: Anthropic
title: How Claude Code works
claim: Describes an agentic harness around models and tools, with context management, project instructions, auto-memory, and saved sessions.
limit: Contextual adaptation and persistent instructions do not establish universal or immediate updates to underlying model weights.

title: Is my data used for model training? - Consumer accounts
claim: Describes consumer model-improvement choices, explicit opt-ins, feedback handling, and specified safety-review uses.

author: Anthropic
title: Is my data used for model training? - Commercial accounts
claim: States that commercial inputs and outputs are not used for model training by default, with explicit feedback or separately authorized sharing capable of creating exceptions.
limit: Does not make every feedback mechanism identical or replace review of the actual agreement, account, authentication route, and program.

author: Wikimedia contributors
title: Research:Wikistats metrics/Active editors
claim: Defines the metric as registered, non-bot editors with at least five edits in a given month, including redirect-page edits.
limit: Not an all-time count of unique human contributors, registered accounts, or every kind of Wikimedia participation.

author: Wikimedia contributors
title: Research:Newly registered user

limit: Registration does not prove editing, unique personhood, or a contribution to a knowledge commons.

title: Nonrivalry and the Economics of Data
claim: Models simultaneous use of data by multiple firms, gains from nonrival use, and inefficiencies from hoarding. American Economic Review 110(9): 2819-58.
limit: Model-dependent welfare results, not a claim that unrestricted sharing is always beneficial or will finance its own stewardship.
